nodes.label: Mathematics in the Age of AI (Terence Tao)
AI Capability Conjecture
nodes.rationale: Template conjecture with free parameters: AI tools will accomplish research-level mathematical tasks with some success rate, cost, and supervision level; weak vs. strong forms determine whether current practices can continue.

nodes.label: Working Hypothesis (Conditional Analysis)
nodes.rationale: Assumes reasonably strong AI capability conjecture is true; enables orthogonal analysis of mathematical goals and values independent of capability debate.

nodes.label: Goals and Values Question (Question 5.1)
nodes.rationale: Core question: what are the precise implicit and explicit goals of mathematical research? Becomes critical under Working Hypothesis to prevent Goodhart's law misalignment.

nodes.label: Problem-Solving Pipeline (Goals 6.1–6.5)
nodes.rationale: Iterative refinement from 'solve problems' to 'solve, verify, communicate, digest, canonicalize'; reveals five implicit stages beyond proof generation.

nodes.label: Proof Scarcity vs. Proof Abundance Transition
nodes.rationale: Under Working Hypothesis, mathematical community will transition from scarcity (current) to abundance (AI-generated proofs); existing institutions designed for scarcity will experience impedance mismatches.

nodes.label: Goodhart's Law in Mathematics
nodes.rationale: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure; AI tools particularly likely to trigger this by optimizing for appearance of output rather than underlying property.

nodes.label: Leiden Declaration on AI and Mathematics
First Proof Project (Independent Assessment)
nodes.rationale: Controlled evaluation of frontier AI models on genuinely novel research-level problems; second batch: 7 of 10 problems received passing grades from at least one system.

edges.rationale: Both address the challenge of scaling from partial progress to complete delivery; Tao's proof abundance scenario parallels FrontierChallenge's finding that high Avg. Scores do not guarantee Pass Rates.

Both decompose scientific work into multi-stage pipelines; Tao's 5-stage problem-solving pipeline (proof generation → verification → exposition → publication → canonicalization) parallels FrontierChallenge's multi-artifact contract evaluation.

hyperedges.label: Mathematical Practice, Values, and AI Impact
hyperedges.rationale: These four concepts together articulate Tao's central argument: AI forces mathematics to make explicit its implicit goals (pipeline), which risk misalignment (Goodhart's law) under abundance (scarcity→abundance transition), requiring community reflection on values.
